_note: The big sweep (sweep-plan.json) mounts tools into a scratch div, which by-passes the page shell:
the nav, the ad slots, the locale dictionary, the data-libs preload and the router never run.
These rows drive tools on their real URL instead, one page load each, so drive.mjs is called
without a "tool" key and mounts into the page's own #tool-root.
It cannot be one background sweep: every row needs its own navigation, and a navigation destroys
the JS context that would be running the sweep. So this file is a checklist the operator walks
one page at a time (docs/TESTING.md, section 4).
expect* keys are asserted by drive.mjs run(): strings that must appear in the preview iframe,
the output area or a field value. locale rows are checked with d.localeInfo() instead.

pages._why: the flagship page: shell + pdf-lib + pdf.js preload + real drop zone + download

proves the dictionary reaches the widget panel, not just the chrome. Two strings, because they come from two different layers: "Herunterladen" is the result row's own download button (w.download, which used to be silently replaced by the English table) and "Stufe" is a settings-field label. drive.mjs only scans the preview iframe, the output area, field values and .file-row/.result-card — so the earlier expectation "komprimieren" could never be satisfied here: that word lives in the h1, which check-locale-leak.mjs asserts statically for all 13 locales.

calculators have no download; the rendered number is the whole result. The strings are read off what /zh/ renders (身高/体重 are the field labels, 22.9 is 70 / 1.75² to the one decimal the tool quotes). An earlier version of this row asked for "22.96" and "BMI", both of which were wrong: the value is one-decimal and the label is translated, so there is no bare "BMI" in the output. Known leak on the same page, asserted nowhere because it is not a bug in the harness: the band badges ("under < 18.5", "obese ≥ 30") and "you are inside the range" are literals in calc.js that never reach the dictionary, so they render English on the most translated locale the site has. See docs/TESTING.md, gap list.

pages.text: Hola mundo, esto es una prueba de contador de palabras para verificar la herramienta.
pages._why: live count without a button, on a real Spanish page. "14" is the true word count of that sentence (the plan used to say 12, which was a guess and passed nothing), and it is asserted glued to its label because "14" on its own also matches the "1493% unique" that the same line renders — an expectation that any output satisfies is worse than none. The label being English here is the known widget-layer gap (the tools call 343 distinct w keys and each locale authors 56), not a regression; when that layer gets translated this string becomes "Palabras14" and the row must be updated with it.

the separator is the test: a German visitor must read 607,53 — a comma, not the English 607.53 the tool used to print whatever the browser's own locale said. Run against the same defaults on /en/ in the same build, the two pages render 607,53 / 1.871,19 / 21.871,19 and 607.53 / 1,871.19 / 21,871.19, so the difference is the site's locale, not the machine's. English grouping would also match a Japanese page, which is why this row is German.
vendor library (qrcode-generator) is loaded through data-libs on the page, not by the driver
the slowest raster tool, on its real URL, with the multi-file zip path; rafShim because a hidden driver tab gets no animation frames and pdf.js paces rendering with rAF
the English 404 page, not a redirect to a locale
a locale-prefixed unknown path must serve the Japanese 404 page

routing._what: the root always opens the English home, whatever the environment: each case sets a country and/or a th_locale cookie, then visits / and must land on /en/ with English in the header
GET /__geo?country=DE sets the dev_country cookie and redirects to /, which still lands on /en/ — the IP no longer changes the entry language
a non-English th_locale cookie does not redirect the root: set th_locale=ja, visit /, stay on /en/ (the cookie is inert for routing now)
the manual header language menu is the only way to change language: click 中文 -> /zh/ with a Chinese header; in-site links stay locale-prefixed so the choice persists by URL, not by auto-redirect
GET /api/geo still answers {country} from the platform header; it now feeds only the GDPR consent banner, never the language

production hosts issue a server redirect / -> /en/ (vercel.json permanent 308; dist/_redirects 301). The local dev server uses the client fallback in router.js, so the redirect is asserted statically by check-routing.mjs (R4/R5), not by a dev-server HTTP status

not_scriptable: window.print() in html-to-pdf blocks the tab: the preview is asserted in the sweep, the dialog needs a human
the real AdSense loader and a real CMP consent dialog (ads are off by default locally — ENABLE_ADS=false renders no ad DOM)
an actual iOS Safari or Android browser: showSaveFilePicker, clipboard write and MediaRecorder are unverified
a real visitor IP: the geo guess here is the ?country= parameter, not MaxMind
